decision: Classify the lot as short-dated and freshness-noncompliant, not expired.
Treat the MRL failure as a commercial freshness issue requiring Freshness Hold and separate exception/disposition analysis; do not infer a safety failure or recall from short dating alone.
Recognize that the two initial product readings above 41°F triggered Temperature Hold and expanded sampling.
Maintain Temperature Hold for all 240 cases because expanded sampling still contains out-of-spec readings and Q&R has not issued technical disposition.
Route technical time/temperature evaluation and any release, restricted disposition, or rejection decision to the Director Q&R or delegated Q&R authority.

If Northstar considers accepting the R3 short-dated product after the temperature concern is technically resolved, require a lot/quantity-specific Freshness Exception with Merchandising Manager and Director Q&R approval and a written reason for the retroactive request; any safety concern remains non-waivable.
Synthesize the shipment status as held pending authorized Q&R disposition, with the commercial freshness branch still open and no declared recall.
